basis: Progressive leukodystrophy with dementia and polycystic bone lesions causing recurrent fractures define the disease.
Trichomonas infection defines the disease; the prostate is outside the anatomical axes. Urinary tract damage is not established.
Hypomyelinating leukodystrophy with ataxia and hypodontia defines this subtype; teeth belong to gastrointestinal. Parental optional hypogonadism is insufficient.
Craniotubular skeletal dysplasia; visual impairment reported in 5/5 supports ocular involvement. Hearing loss and cardiac defects each occur in only 1/5.
Unilateral renal agenesis is a defining component; seminal vesicle and ejaculatory duct abnormalities are outside the axes.
Sarcomatoid variant of cutaneous basal cell carcinoma; skin is the tumour's origin.
Myocardial infarction injures the inferolateral heart wall.
Multiple serrated colonic polyps define this gastrointestinal condition; subsequent cancer risk adds no axis.
Thiamine metabolism/transport defects; encephalopathy, seizures and neurodegeneration occur in most major subtypes. Anemia and deafness are subtype-specific.
Acquired metabolic disorder defined by ethanol fermentation within the bladder; intoxication and systemic organ injury are absent.
Severe intellectual disability and delayed sexual maturation define the syndrome, supporting neurologic and endocrine axes; proportionate dwarfism alone does not establish skeletal disease.
Malignant neoplasm located in the urinary bladder dome; bladder belongs to the renal axis.
Glaucoma is an ocular disease causing optic nerve damage; the underlying secondary cause is unspecified.
Persistent frontal sinus inflammation affects the upper airway. Infectious, allergic and structural causes vary; infection or immune mediation is not universal.
Childhood chorea with structural striatal abnormalities is a neurologic disorder; occasional anxiety adds no axis.
Severe developmental disability and ocular anomalies define disease; thin skin/sparse hair in 4/4 and respiratory failure in 80-99% support skin and pulmonary involvement.
Von Willebrand factor deficiency or dysfunction causes a coagulation disorder. Bleeding sites do not establish separate organ damage.
Seizures/hypotonia and acne occur in 30-79%; seborrheic dermatitis is characteristic. Anemia/bone changes are <30%; nonspecific immune annotation does not establish immunodeficiency.
Trabecular variant of thyroid follicular carcinoma; thyroid tumour origin establishes the endocrine axis.
Axonal neuropathy; hearing loss in 3/7 (~43%); pes cavus in 80-99% and scoliosis/kyphosis in 30-79%. Elevated transaminases alone do not establish liver disease.
Inherited abnormal albumin binding alters circulating thyroid hormone measurements; patients are euthyroid, without intrinsic thyroid injury or other organ damage.
Malignancy occupies the major salivary glands, which belong to gastrointestinal. Lymphoma is only one possible histology, not the umbrella mechanism.
Hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction and neurodevelopmental disability define disease; scoliosis occurs in 150/180 (~83%). Feeding difficulty alone does not establish GI damage.
Herniation of intracranial contents through a frontal skull defect defines encephalocele, involving neural tissue and calvarial bone.
Chondrodysplasia and myotonia from neuromuscular junction hyperexcitability define disease; visual impairment in 80-99% and cataract in 30-79% support ocular involvement.
